# Limit answers of plans we have no account for

Samples of the subscription limit answers of plans the author does not have (EKR-41). How such answers are found and how a sample is made from one is in [`docs/sessions/limits.md`](../../../docs/sessions/limits.md), "Answers of plans we have no account for". In short: each file is written by us in the shape of a public answer, not copied; ids, emails and tokens are left out, the values and reset times are made up (January 2030), and a field the source cut out (`...`) is left out rather than invented.

## What each sample holds

- **Paid Copilot** — `src/limits/copilot-credits.test.ts` keeps synthetic inline samples: the legacy personal/education `remaining` shape from [paseo#8478](https://github.com/getpaseo/paseo/issues/8478), and the token-billed Enterprise fields from [ghcp-spend-tray's JsonModels.cs](https://github.com/DamianEdwards/ghcp-spend-tray/blob/main/src/GHCPSpendTray.Core/JsonModels.cs) (consulted 2026-11-12). The latter tool has [validated Enterprise only](https://github.com/DamianEdwards/ghcp-spend-tray/issues/18); these samples are not live evidence for personal AI credits. The billing sample follows [GitHub's personal AI-credit report](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/billing/usage#get-billing-ai-credit-usage-report-for-a-user), with `Copilot AI Credits` as product; values and dates are made up.
- **Copilot Business, spent** — only `quota_snapshots.premium_interactions` with `unlimited: true` and `percent_remaining: 100` next to `remaining: 0`, `entitlement: 0`, `credits_used` above zero and `overage_permitted: false`; the reset is `quota_reset_date`. No raw Business answer with this contradiction was found (`gh search issues 'quota_snapshots premium_interactions'`, 2026-11-17): the fields are the source's summary of its parsed reading, our spend differs from its 1937, and `chat`/`completions` are left out. The source's older fixture has the same shape with `overage_permitted: true` and counts as unlimited; the tests set that field on this sample.

- **OpenCode Go** — `opencode-go-200.json` has `usage.rolling`, `weekly`, `monthly` in the shape of the MIT [t3code reader](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/blob/main/packages/provider-opencode/src/server/usageLimits.ts), consulted 2026-11-11; values and dates are synthetic, and `0.5` deliberately stays 0.5 percent until the scale is verified live. `opencode-go-401.json` follows the `authentication_error` / `api_key_expired` shape reported in [t3code#21625](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/issues/21625), with a made-up message. `opencode-go-403.json` is `{}`: the reader documents the status as no Go subscription but no body, so no body fields are invented. Status comes from the file name. `src/opencode/go.test.ts` reads all three. The three windows are described in [Go's documentation](https://opencode.ai/docs/go/); the relative reset text comes from [opencode#49170](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/49170).

- **ChatGPT Edu seat** — `plan_type: "education"`, the five-hour and the weekly window, `credits.balance: null` with `has_credits: true`, and `spend_control: {reached: false, individual_limit: null}`; the source's ids were removed there already. `monthly-usage` has only `balance_unit: "credit"`, `effective_monthly_limit` (`limit`, `enforcement_mode: "HARD_CAP"`, `limit_mode: "amount_credits"`) and `current_month_usage`; the source asked it with `?supports_usage_limit_modes=true`. Our cap and use differ from the source's (7000 and 0 there). The same issue names a Team seat's sample with `spend_control.reached: true` (`codex_usage_team_spend_cap.json`); the tests set `reached` on the Edu one instead.
- **ChatGPT Pro** — one weekly window in `primary_window` (`limit_window_seconds: 604800`), `secondary_window: null`: Pro has no five-hour window. The source's `user_id`, `account_id` and `email` are left out.
- **Claude Max** — `five_hour` and `seven_day` filled, `seven_day_opus`, `seven_day_sonnet` and `seven_day_cowork` `null`; the model's week is the `weekly_scoped` entry of `limits[]` (`scope.model.display_name: "Fable"`), Each `limits[]` entry has `group`, `severity`, `resets_at`, `scope` and `is_active`, as in opencodex#8110 (the first two sources cut out `resets_at`); `is_active` is set only on the entry holding the account now, here the spent model week, while `session` and `weekly_all` apply all the same. Other top-level keys of the answer were omitted in the sources.
- **Claude Ultra** — `"five_hour": null` and no `session` entry in `limits[]`: a verified Ultra account has no five-hour limit. `seven_day` has the dollar fields the source shows. The sources show only `kind`, `percent` and the model of the `limits[]` entries, so `group`, `severity`, `is_active` and `resets_at` are absent; the top-level `seven_day_*` keys were not shown.
- **Claude Team/Enterprise** — `"seven_day": null`; `limits[]` has `session` and `weekly_scoped`, no `weekly_all`. The source shows only these two keys: `five_hour` and the entries' `resets_at` are absent.
- **Codex 429** — `status`, `headers` and `body` of one answer. `X-Codex-Active-Limit: premium` names a limit that has no headers of its own, while the full `X-Codex-Primary-*` (100 %, 300 minutes) and `X-Codex-Secondary-*` (53 %, 10080 minutes) families are there. codex 0.165 reads only the active family and writes an empty `premium` snapshot into the rollout's `token_count` (EKR-30); its turn ends with the usage limit.

## Who reads them

- `src/limits/chatgpt.test.ts` — the Pro sample through `chatGptLimits`, its zero `rate_limit_reset_credits` too (BTN-1269).
- `src/limits/chatgpt-seat.test.ts` — the two Edu samples through `chatGptLimits` and `askChatGpt`, and the Pro one as a personal plan.
- `src/codex/rollout.test.ts` — the 429 body as the error of a failed turn.
- `src/limits/copilot-credits.test.ts` — the spent Business sample through `copilotLimits` and `askCopilot` (EKR-133).
- `src/limits/usage.test.ts` — the `limits[]` of the three Claude samples through `modelWeeksOf`, alone and as the `usage_report` of a `/usage` stream: Even Keel does not ask `/api/oauth/usage` itself, but the CLI's `/usage` message carries the same rows (BTN-805), the plan's windows included (EKR-131).
